newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's cedes stake in agro-industry firm.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's cedes stake in agro-industry firm.

text.p: Morocco's largest private ONA Group ceded its 86.25 percent in maize derivatives producer SOMADIM to British-Belgian group Amylum, a statement issued by the group said on Friday.
"ONA's subsidiary Cosumar ceded its 86.25 percent in Somadim to Amylum group," the statement said.
It said the accord was signed on October 30, 1996 but gave no details on the value of the cession.

"The move was in line with ONA's strategic plan which aims at focusing its activity in the future on the core businesses which are mining, finance, international and agro-industry sectors," a market analyst said.
Established in Casablanca in 1965, Societe Marocaine des Derives Industriels du Mais (SOMADIM) registered a turnover of 96.5 million dirhams ($11.2 million) in 1995.
It posted a net profit of 8.5 million dirhams in the same period.
Amylum already holds minor stakes in SOMADIM, ONA said.
With a production capacity of 100 tonnes per day, SOMADIM has a capital of 9.0 million dirhams and employs a staff of 112, according to the latest figures.
ONA, with holdings in more than 100 firms, showed a 20.6 percent rise in its consolidated net profit to $37.7 million in the first half 1996 compared with the first six months of of 1995.
Among the 47 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, ONA and COSUMAR were last traded respectively at 500 dirhams and 685 dirhams per share.
